newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG army on alert to protect sacked commander.
newsitem.headline: PNG army on alert to protect sacked commander.

text.p: Fully-armed soldiers were on alert at Papua New Guinea's main army headquarters Murray Barracks on Monday following reports police have been ordered to arrest sacked army boss Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok.
Singirok, who led an army revolt in March which forced prime minister Sir Julius Chan to step aside, lives inside Murray Barracks and is still de facto commander of the army.

Defence force chief of staff Colonel Reg Renagi told Reuters the army was on alert and would not allow any police to enter the barracks to arrest Singirok. He said it was illegal for police to enter the barracks without army authorisation.
Fully armed soldiers were manning the main gates to Murray Barracks, as well as Singirok's residence high on a hill inside the barracks.
Police sources on Monday said orders had been given to arrest Singirok, but the charges remain unclear.

In March, Singirok demanded Chan resign within 48 hours over a plan to hire 70 African mercenaries to help end a secessionist revolt on resource-rich Bougainville island, 800 km (500 miles) northeast of Port Moresby.
Singirok said the US$36 million mercenary deal was corrupt.

Chan sacked Singirok, sparking an army revolt which eventually saw Chan step aside pending the outcome of a judicial inquiry into the mercenary deal. Singirok has said the inquiry, which ends on May 30, will be a whitewash.
